raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Reuse the MoE framework's `workspace2` for FlashInfer CUTLASS scratch to avoid large per-call allocations during serving. Addresses [#60471](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60471); this targets a post-startup OOM and does not claim to fix the profiling-time capacity failure in [#47127](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47127).

## Claims

- Reserve CUTLASS scratch during profiling through `workspace_shapes` and reuse the framework's shared allocation.
- Keep scratch disjoint from output; report zero for the unused `workspace13` shape.
- Include gathered DP input, the autotuning minimum and elastic DP limits via `fi_moe_largest_bucket`, with logical dimensions and quantization dtypes matching the kernel.
- Retain compatibility with FlashInfer versions lacking caller-owned CUTLASS workspace support.

## Validation

Revision `0dad84737f` was validated on B200 by applying its production patch to the pinned image below. GPU correctness, matched serving and full GSM8K evaluation are complete.

- **GPU regression/correctness: 174 passed, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped.** This includes 12 BF16/NVFP4 cases exercising the real framework allocator, capacity for gathered/elastic DP, reuse after locking, output/scratch non-overlap and CUDA graph replay with changed inputs. The remaining cases cover the capability gate, SwiGLU parameters, NVFP4 and FP8 correctness.
- **Matched serving on 8× B200:** the unpatched control reproduced a 19.99 GiB CUDA OOM. The previous persistent-workspace implementation and both `workspace2` runs each completed all 5 / 320 / 1,280 requests at concurrency 1 / 64 / 256 (1,605 total).

| Output tokens/s | Previous persistent workspace | Framework workspace2, run 1 | Framework workspace2, run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Concurrency 1 | 127.27 | 129.88 | 128.48 |
| Concurrency 64 | 5,223.66 | 5,183.24 | 5,227.70 |
| Concurrency 256 | 12,739.68 | 12,651.67 | 12,784.89 |

The revised runs span 5,183.24–5,227.70 tok/s at concurrency 64 and 12,651.67–12,784.89 at concurrency 256. No throughput speedup is claimed.

Both workspace2 serving logs confirm allocation through the MoE framework, completed CUDA graph capture and no CUTLASS workspace-sizing fallback or OOM. KV capacity remained 2,813,184 tokens per rank, matching the persistent-workspace control.

**Full GSM8K:** lm-eval `0.4.11`, 1,319 questions, 5-shot, same DP8/EP/CUDA-graph settings. Each arm completed 1,319 HTTP-200 completion requests, with zero empty responses, non-200 responses, OOMs or CUTLASS workspace-sizing fallbacks.

| Exact-match accuracy ± standard error | Unpatched | Framework workspace2 | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Flexible extract | 93.404% ± 0.684 pp (1,232/1,319) | 93.025% ± 0.702 pp (1,227/1,319) | −0.379 pp |
| Strict match | 92.722% ± 0.716 pp (1,223/1,319) | 92.191% ± 0.739 pp (1,216/1,319) | −0.531 pp |

The observed decreases are smaller than each run's reported standard error. This single comparison does not establish statistical equivalence or rule out a small accuracy regression.

Stack: `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f620665f46d536e42698e5649fa9eebc51e2b71ff0d5f09ee11ea7674d4c655e`, vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev616+g1a001d584`, FlashInfer `0.7.0.post1`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`. Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4`. TP=1, DP=8, EP and CUDA graphs enabled; memory utilization 0.9, max-model-len 9216, max-num-batched-tokens 16384, `flashinfer_cutlass` MoE, FLASHINFER attention. AIPerf used 8,000 input / 1,000 output tokens with unchanged flags across arms.

The test tree was taken from `630e30d8f7` with the revised `test_flashinfer_moe.py` from `0dad84737f`; imports resolved to the patched installed package. The executed test selection was:

```bash
python3 -m pytest -v -rsfE -p no:cacheprovider --continue-on-collection-errors \
  tests/utils_/test_flashinfer_utils.py::test_cutlass_workspace_requires_both_apis \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe.py::test_flashinfer_workspace_reused_after_lock \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe.py::test_flashinfer_swigluoai_params_are_forwarded \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_moe.py::test_flashinfer_fp4_moe_no_graph \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py::test_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp8_no_graph
```

These results validate the production patch on the pinned image, rather than a build of the entire newer PR base.

The evaluation invocation below normalizes the local model path and service port; the server used the served-model name `nemotron-super-v3-120b-a12b`:

```bash
lm_eval --model openai-completions \
  --model_args 'base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,model=nemotron-super-v3-120b-a12b,tokenizer=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,tokenized_requests=false,max_length=9216,eos_string=<|im_end|>' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 1319 \
  --output_path ./gsm8k-results --log_samples
```

<details>
<summary>Serving reproduction</summary>

The original nightly tag was removed from Docker Hub. Pull the same base
image by digest:

```bash
docker run --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f620665f46d536e42698e5649fa9eebc51e2b71ff0d5f09ee11ea7674d4c655e \
  nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 9216 \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 --moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 16384
```

Send 8,000-input-token / 1,000-output-token requests, ignoring EOS, at
concurrency 1 / 64 / 256 with 5 / 320 / 1,280 requests respectively.
The recorded results above used AIPerf. This equivalent vLLM benchmark command
is provided for reproduction but has not been run for this draft:

```bash
for concurrency in 1 64 256; do
  .venv/bin/vllm bench serve \
    --backend vllm --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
    --model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8000 --random-output-len 1000 \
    --max-concurrency "$concurrency" \
    --num-prompts "$((concurrency == 1 ? 5 : concurrency * 5))" \
    --request-rate inf --ignore-eos
done
```

</details>

## Details

Without caller-owned scratch, FlashInfer allocates and releases large GEMM buffers on each MoE invocation. That transient allocation contributes to memory profiling but must be allocated again during serving, where fragmentation can cause an OOM despite substantial reserved-but-unused memory.

In response to review, `workspace_shapes` now reports CUTLASS scratch in `workspace2`. The framework allocates output storage and scratch simultaneously. `workspace13` reports zero because the backend does not use it; the framework still reserves the output. This removes the separate persistent-resource allocation and lets sequential operations share the framework's scratch storage.

Sizing uses logical hidden/intermediate dimensions, including unpacked NVFP4 K, gated/non-gated N and packed weight dtypes. Size queries are cached. The byte capacity is rounded up to the framework's workspace dtype. Different token counts can produce different scratch offsets after the output reservation; backing storage is shared and captured graph addresses remain stable after locking.

Older FlashInfer versions and size-query failures retain per-call allocation and its original fragmentation risk. Inputs exceeding the profiled capacity follow the framework's normal locked-workspace checks. No scheduler or model-runner changes are required.

This updates the existing PR following review. Draft [#60617](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60617) independently overlaps with the workspace2 approach; no additional PR is being opened. The CUTLASS API comes from [FlashInfer #4057](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4057); TRTLLM-gen integration is separate in [#62948](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62948).

AI assistance was used to implement the change, prepare tests and draft this description.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. GPU regression and matched serving passed; full GSM8K results and their limitations are reported above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "max_num_tokens, dp_size, elastic_ep_max_dp_size, workspace_rows",
+    [(32, 1, None, 8192), (32, 2, None, 8192), (4096, 2, 4, 16384)],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("activation", [MoEActivation.SILU, MoEActivation.RELU2_NO_MUL])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("quant_dtype", [None, "nvfp4"])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_flashinfer_workspace_reused_after_lock(
+    max_num_tokens,
+    dp_size,
+    elastic_ep_max_dp_size,
+    workspace_rows,
+    activation,
+    quant_dtype,
+    workspace_init,
+    monkeypatch,
+):
+    """Framework scratch must survive locking and graph replay without aliasing."""
+    parallel = FusedMoEParallelConfig.make_no_parallel()
+    parallel.dp_size = dp_size
+    config = FusedMoEConfig(
+        num_experts=8,
+        experts_per_token=2,
+        hidden_dim=256,
+        intermediate_size=512,
+        num_local_experts=8,
+        num_logical_experts=8,
+        activation=activation,
+        device="cuda",
+        moe_parallel_config=parallel,
+        in_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        routing_method=RoutingMethodType.TopK,
+        max_num_tokens=max_num_tokens,
+        elastic_ep_max_dp_size=elastic_ep_max_dp_size,
+    )
+    max_rows = max_num_tokens * dp_size
+    x = torch.randn(max_rows, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+    w1 = (
+        torch.randn(
+            8,
+            512 * (2 if activation.is_gated else 1),
+            256,
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+        / 10
+    )
+    w2 = torch.randn(8, 256, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 10
+    quant_config = FusedMoEQuantConfig.make()
+    if quant_dtype is not None:
+        w1, w2, quant_config = make_test_quant_config(
+            8,
+            512,
+            256,
+            in_dtype=x.dtype,
+            quant_dtype=quant_dtype,
+            block_shape=None,
+            per_act_token_quant=False,
+            make_gate=activation.is_gated,
+        )
+    layers = [
+        FusedMoEKernel(
+            MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular(),
+            FlashInferExperts(config, quant_config),
+        )
+        for _ in range(2)
+    ]
+    ids = torch.tensor([0, 1], device="cuda").expand(max_rows, 2)
+    weights = torch.full((max_rows, 2), 0.5, device="cuda")
+    expected_nbytes = fi_moe.flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe_workspace_size(
+        workspace_rows,
+        256,
+        512,
+        8,
+        2,
+        x_dtype=torch.uint8 if quant_dtype == "nvfp4" else x.dtype,
+        weight_dtype=torch.long if quant_dtype == "nvfp4" else w1.dtype,
+        output_dtype=x.dtype,
+        activation_type=activation_to_flashinfer_type(activation),
+        device=x.device,
+    )
+    buffers = []
+    call_args: dict = {}
+    kernel = fi_moe.flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe
+
+    def record_workspace(**kwargs):
+        call_args.clear()
+        call_args.update(kwargs)
+        scratch = kwargs["workspace_buffer"]
+        output = kwargs["output"]
+        buffers.append(scratch)
+        assert scratch.dtype == torch.uint8 and scratch.ndim == 1
+        assert scratch.nbytes >= expected_nbytes
+        # The common workspace reserves the output before workspace2, even
+        # when prepare/finalize supplies an external output allocation.
+        assert scratch.storage_offset() >= output.nbytes
+        assert (
+            scratch.data_ptr() + scratch.nbytes <= output.data_ptr()
+            or output.data_ptr() + output.nbytes <= scratch.data_ptr()
+        )
+        return kernel(**kwargs)
+
+    def run(layer, rows):
+        return layer.apply(
+            hidden_states=x[:rows],
+            w1=w1,
+            w2=w2,
+            topk_weights=weights[:rows],
+            topk_ids=ids[:rows],
+            activation=activation,
+            global_num_experts=8,
+            expert_map=None,
+            apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+        )
+
+    def check_reference(output):
+        reference = torch.empty_like(output)
+        kernel(**{**call_args, "workspace_buffer": None, "output": reference})
+        torch.testing.assert_close(output, reference)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(fi_moe, "flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe", record_workspace)
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+        check_reference(run(layers[0], max_rows))
+        manager = current_workspace_manager()
+        manager.lock()
+        storage_ptr = manager.get_simultaneous(((1,), torch.uint8))[0].data_ptr()
+        for layer, rows in [(layers[1], 1), (layers[0], 17), (layers[1], max_rows)]:
+            check_reference(run(layer, rows))
+
+        stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            run(layers[0], 16)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+            output = run(layers[0], 16)
+        for _ in range(2):
+            x[:16].normal_(std=0.1)
+            graph.replay()
+            check_reference(output)
+        assert all(b.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == storage_ptr for b in buffers)
+
+

Updated in `0dad84737f`: CUTLASS scratch now comes from the MoE framework’s `workspace2`, and the unused `workspace13` shape is zero. Scratch remains separate from the output.

On the same pinned image with 8× B200, the unpatched control reproduced the 19.99 GiB OOM; both revised serving runs completed all 1,605 requests. All 174 GPU tests passed, including numerical correctness, locked workspace reuse, and CUDA graph replay.

Full GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot): 93.40% stock → 93.03% workspace2, a −0.38 pp difference versus reported standard errors of about 0.7 pp per run. Both completed all requests with no empty responses, HTTP errors or OOMs. This single comparison cannot rule out a small accuracy regression. Full results are in the PR description.
